title: Classical, Steinitz & Gambits
intro: Answer 3...Bc5 with 4.c3 and d4, meet 3...d6 with 4.d4, avoid the Noah's Ark trap against 4...d6, and counter 3...f5 with 4.Nc3.
variation: e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1b5 f8c5, e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1b5 d7d6, e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1b5 f7f5

lessons.title: Meeting 3...Bc5
lessons.summary: Build a commanding centre with 4.c3 and 5.d4.

steps.text: In the Classical Defence, Black develops 3...Bc5 before playing ...a6 or ...Nf6.
Prepare to build a strong pawn centre with d4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.c3 so d4 comes with tempo against the c5 bishop.
steps.ifRight: Now White threatens to take over the centre.

steps.text: Black develops and attacks e4 with 4...Nf6.
Strike in the centre at once.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.d4 to hit the c5 bishop and claim the centre.

steps.text: Recapture to keep two central pawns side by side.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.cxd4: the bishop on c5 is attacked and White owns the centre.
steps.ifRight: White has a commanding centre with e4 and d4.

steps.text: Black checks with 6...Bb4+. Block cleanly while developing a piece.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Bd2: after 7...Bxd2+ 8.Nbxd2, your pieces develop smoothly.
steps.ifRight: If Black trades bishops, Nbxd2 leaves White with a big centre and fast development.

lessons.title: Steinitz & Noah's Ark Trap
lessons.summary: Push 4.d4 against 3...d6, and play c3 first against 4...d6.

steps.text: In the Steinitz Defence, Black defends e5 passively with 3...d6.

steps.ifWrong: Play 4.d4 to pressure e5 and gain central space.
steps.ifRight: With ...a6 not played, d4 is completely safe and strong.

steps.text: Protect e4 and finish queenside development.
steps.ifRight: White enjoys a big space advantage and easy development.

steps.text: Watch out when Black plays 4...d6 after 3...a6 4.Ba4. Playing 5.d4 straight away walks into the Noah's Ark trap after 5...b5 6.Bb3 Nxd4.
Avoid the trap by giving your bishop an escape square on c2 first.
steps.hint: Play c3 or castle before pushing d4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.c3 (or 5.O-O) so ...b5 can be met with Bc2.
steps.ifRight: Now your bishop can drop back to c2 and d4 is safe next move.

feedback.d2d4: 5.d4 lets Black play 5...b5 6.Bb3 Nxd4 7.Nxd4 exd4 8.Qxd4 c5, trapping your bishop after ...c4.

steps.text: The Schliemann Gambit (3...f5) tries to attack e4 and open the f-file.
Defend e4 and develop a piece at the same time.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Nc3: taking on f5 lets Black gain central space with ...e4.
steps.ifRight: This is the cleanest and strongest answer to 3...f5.

steps.hint: Take back on e4 with the c3 knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Nxe4: if Black pushes 5...d5, 6.Nxe5 hits hard.
steps.ifRight: White stands clearly better against Black's weakened kingside.

steps.text: Here Black played the Bird Defence with 3...Nd4. Answer the double attack.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Nxd4: after 4...exd4 5.O-O, Black's pawns are weak and White leads in development.
steps.ifRight: White castles next and attacks d4 with c3 or d3.

steps.ifWrong: Play 5.O-O to get your king safe before challenging d4.
steps.ifRight: White follows with d3, Bc4 or c3 with a strong position.
